text: Combining OI with funding (CoinMarketMan heuristic, untested): rising OI with high positive funding means longs are paying shorts to hold, so the trend may be better to fade than chase; OI and funding together indicate whether crowd positioning is sustainable. (low confidence)

text: Elevated basis or funding is a crowding gauge, not a timing tool. BIS finds high crypto carry predicts future price crashes and that rising carry goes with a rising price of crash-risk insurance. CoinMarketMan reads rising OI plus extreme funding plus a nearby liquidation cluster as an overcrowded market at risk of a sharp reversal, while saying it does not give the timing. (medium confidence)
keywords: Funding and open interest divergence and basis

text: Funding-rate arbitrage is not risk-free and earns mostly from convergence. He et al.: the perp cash-and-carry has no predetermined unwind date; in their decomposition price convergence dominates strategy returns while funding payments play a minor, diminishing role; their no-arbitrage result is conditional on exchange solvency. BIS: the arbitrage side is risky because margins spike and liquidations hit in drawdowns, which keeps arbitrage capital scarce. (medium confidence)
keywords: Funding and open interest divergence and basis

text: Price-versus-OI read (a descriptive heuristic, not a forecast): price up and OI up = new longs, trend confirmed; price up and OI down = short covering, weaker rally; price down and OI up = new shorts, bearish conviction building; price down and OI down = longs exiting or liquidated, possible exhaustion. CoinMarketMan adds that the rate of change in OI matters more than its level and that sharp OI spikes or drops are events. (medium confidence)
keywords: Funding and open interest divergence and basis

text: Funding mostly follows price instead of leading it. Presto Research (BTC on Binance, roughly 2021 to 2024): the 7-day change in annualised funding explains 12.5% of contemporaneous price-change variance, but at lag T to T+1 correlation and R-squared are about zero; it concludes single-asset price changes cannot be reliably predicted from funding-rate changes alone. He et al. likewise find trailing spot returns positively predict the perp-spot deviation. (medium confidence)
keywords: Funding and open interest divergence and basis

text: Venue differences matter for cross-venue divergence. BitMEX's own Q3 2025 study (BitMEX, Binance, Hyperliquid) says BitMEX funding was the most stable and Hyperliquid showed much higher funding volatility. The study is BitMEX partner content and promotes the company. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-14)
